claims.text: Pre-exposure Q235 steel has an unaltered native passive oxide film.
Pre-equilibration in dilute chloride solution promotes controlled chloride adsorption on Q235 steel.
The chloride pretreatment produces a distinct adsorbed chloride-ion layer at the steel/solution interface.
Adsorbed chloride ions disrupt the integrity of the native passive oxide film.
Disruption of the passive film reduces charge-transfer resistance.
Disruption of the passive film facilitates localized breakdown and pitting corrosion.
Elevated temperature enhances ion mobility or kinetics.
Elevated temperature destabilizes the passive film and accelerates corrosion-related degradation.
Chloride-pretreated specimens will have lower charge-transfer resistance than untreated specimens.
Chloride-pretreated specimens will exhibit an earlier onset of pitting than untreated specimens.
Earlier pitting will be evidenced by a lower potential in potentiodynamic polarization measurements.
Chloride-pretreated specimens will exhibit altered EIS spectra relative to untreated specimens.
The proposed mechanism applies in 3.5 wt.% NaCl from approximately 25 °C to 70 °C.
Additional aggressive species or mechanical stresses may change the governing degradation mechanism.
Untreated Q235 steel tested under otherwise identical NaCl and temperature conditions provides the experimental control.
EIS, potentiodynamic polarization, and XPS can be used to compare electrochemical behavior and verify chloride presence and film composition.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field requires both statistically similar electrochemical behavior and failure to confirm a distinct chloride layer for decisive falsification, whereas the formal falsification rule uses 'and/or,' implying that either result may independently falsify the hypothesis.
